title: Tamino mein! O welch ein Glück!
subtitle: Pamina and Tamino, the two Armed Men and the chorus: from the finale of Die Zauberflöte, Act 2

passages.label: Tamino mein! · Hier sind die Schreckenspforten · Ich werde aller Orten an deiner Seite sein
Spiel' du die Zauberflöte an · Es schnitt in einer Zauberstunde · Nun komm und spiel die Flöte an
Wir wandeln durch des Tones Macht (with the Armed Men, to the fermata)
The march through fire and water · Wir wandelten durch Feuergluthen · Ihr Götter, welch ein Augenblick
Triumph, Triumph, du edles Paar! (the chorus from within, Allegro, to the end)

licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages in two chunks, each by two independent readers, with a judge settling every difference and a sweep for the marks, then a fresh check by three proofreaders until clean (one fix: no staccato on the left hand in bar 15); every bar of every part adds up. The Italian translation, the notes printed only for it, and the stage directions are left out. Andante, 3/4, F major, from a one-beat upbeat; the march (“Marsch. Adagio”, 4/4, C major) from bar 86, its flute solo played by the piano as printed; the chorus from within (“Triumph”, Allegro) from bar 114. Bar 113 is a 7/8 bar and bar 114 a one-eighth upbeat, as printed. The chorus German is printed under only some staves; each chorus voice takes the German of the staff singing the same rhythm. The chorus is heard with the piano and has no role here. Playback tempo from complete recordings: the median length of this scene, 7:02, from Haitink 1981 (7:28), Böhm 1964 (7:03), Solti 1969 (7:02), Klemperer 1964 (6:59) and Toscanini 1937 (6:04); Andante ♩ = 74, march ♩ = 40, Allegro ♩ = 113, from the splits of Solti's (at the march) and Haitink's (at the march and at the chorus) tracks.
